jabbok_609.name: Jabbok
jabbok_609.what: A river flowing west into the Jordan, forming a natural boundary in the land of Gilead.
key: Jacob crossed the ford of the Jabbok and wrestled with a man until daybreak (Genesis 32).
Israel took Sihon's land from the Arnon to the Jabbok (Numbers 21).
Moses set the Jabbok as a border for Reuben and Gad (Deuteronomy 3).
Jephthah answered the Ammonite king's claim to the land between the Arnon and the Jabbok (Judges 11).

kiriath-arba_697.name: Kiriath-arba
kiriath-arba_697.what: The older name of Hebron, a city in the hill country of Judah named after Arba of the Anakim.
kiriath-arba_697.today: Hebron, in the southern West Bank.
key: Sarah died at Kiriath-arba, and Abraham mourned for her (Genesis 23).
Jacob returned to his father Isaac at Kiriath-arba, where Isaac died (Genesis 35).
Joshua gave Hebron, formerly Kiriath-arba, to Caleb as his inheritance (Joshua 14).
Judah defeated Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai there (Judges 1).
Some people of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba after the exile (Nehemiah 11).

mesopotamia_790.name: Mesopotamia
mesopotamia_790.what: The land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, homeland of Abraham's family.
mesopotamia_790.today: Mainly modern Iraq, with parts of Syria and Turkey.
key: Abraham's servant traveled to Mesopotamia to find a wife for Isaac (Genesis 24).
Balaam was hired from Pethor in Mesopotamia to curse Israel (Deuteronomy 23).
Othniel delivered Israel from Cushan-rishathaim, king of Mesopotamia (Judges 3).
Jews and converts from Mesopotamia heard the apostles at Pentecost (Acts 2).
Stephen recalled that God appeared to Abraham in Mesopotamia before Haran (Acts 7).

mount_hermon_841.name: Mount Hermon
mount_hermon_841.what: The highest mountain in the region, marking the northern limit of Israel's conquests east of the Jordan.
mount_hermon_841.today: Mount Hermon, on the border of Syria and Lebanon above the Golan Heights.
key: Moses noted that Sidonians called Hermon Sirion and Amorites called it Senir (Deuteronomy 3).
Joshua's conquest reached the valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon (Joshua 11).
Og king of Bashan had ruled as far as Mount Hermon (Joshua 12).
The half-tribe of Manasseh settled from Bashan to Mount Hermon (1 Chronicles 5).

nebo_883.name: Nebo
nebo_883.what: A town east of the Jordan near Mount Nebo, built up by Reuben and later held by Moab.
nebo_883.today: Likely Khirbet al-Mukhayyat, near Mount Nebo in Jordan.
key: The Reubenites rebuilt Nebo and settled there (Numbers 32).
Israel camped in the mountains of Abarim before Nebo (Numbers 33).
Reubenite clans lived from Aroer to Nebo and Baal-meon (1 Chronicles 5).
Isaiah pictured Moab wailing over Nebo (Isaiah 15).
Jeremiah announced judgment on Nebo among the cities of Moab (Jeremiah 48).

taanach_1124.name: Taanach
taanach_1124.what: A Canaanite city on the southern edge of the Jezreel Valley, near Megiddo.
taanach_1124.today: Tell Ta'annek, near Jenin in the northern West Bank.
key: Joshua defeated the king of Taanach (Joshua 12).
Manasseh received Taanach but did not drive out its Canaanites (Judges 1).
Taanach was given to the Levites of Kohath's clan (Joshua 21).
Deborah's song says the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach (Judges 5).
It belonged to one of Solomon's administrative districts (1 Kings 4).

tekoa_1142.name: Tekoa
tekoa_1142.what: A town in the Judean hills south of Bethlehem, on the edge of the wilderness.
tekoa_1142.today: Khirbet Tequ', south of Bethlehem in the West Bank.
key: Joab brought a wise woman from Tekoa to persuade David to recall Absalom (2 Samuel 14).
Rehoboam fortified Tekoa as a defensive city of Judah (2 Chronicles 11).
Jehoshaphat's army marched into the wilderness of Tekoa and God gave victory (2 Chronicles 20).
Jeremiah called for a trumpet blast in Tekoa as disaster approached (Jeremiah 6).
Amos was among the shepherds of Tekoa when he prophesied (Amos 1).

zin_1261.name: Zin
zin_1261.what: A desert region south of Canaan around Kadesh, where Israel wandered and camped.
zin_1261.today: The desert of southern Israel and northeastern Sinai, near Kadesh-barnea.
key: The twelve spies began exploring Canaan from the wilderness of Zin (Numbers 13).
Miriam died at Kadesh in Zin, and Moses struck the rock at Meribah (Numbers 20).
God reminded Moses that he had rebelled in the wilderness of Zin (Numbers 27).
Zin marked the southern border of Canaan and of Judah (Numbers 34).
Judah's southern boundary passed along the wilderness of Zin (Joshua 15).

zoan_1270.name: Zoan
zoan_1270.what: An ancient royal city in the northeastern Nile Delta of Egypt.
zoan_1270.today: San el-Hagar (ancient Tanis), in the northeastern Nile Delta, Egypt.
key: Hebron was built seven years before Zoan in Egypt (Numbers 13).
God worked his wonders against Egypt in the fields of Zoan (Psalms 78).
Isaiah called the princes of Zoan foolish counselors (Isaiah 19).
Judah's envoys went to Zoan seeking Egypt's help (Isaiah 30).
Ezekiel foretold that God would set fire to Zoan (Ezekiel 30).

ar_77.name: Ar
ar_77.what: A chief city of Moab near the Arnon River, given by God to the descendants of Lot.
ar_77.today: Exact site unknown; likely near the Arnon in Jordan.
key: The Amorites' victory song says fire consumed Ar of Moab (Numbers 21).
God told Israel not to harass Moab, for he had given Ar to Lot's descendants (Deuteronomy 2).
Isaiah lamented that Ar of Moab was laid waste in a night (Isaiah 15).

arabia_80.name: Arabia
arabia_80.what: The desert lands east and south of Israel, home to nomadic tribes and trading peoples.
arabia_80.today: The Arabian Peninsula; in Galatians likely the Nabatean region of Jordan and northwestern Saudi Arabia.
key: The kings of Arabia brought gold and silver to Solomon (2 Chronicles 9).
Isaiah delivered an oracle concerning Arabia (Isaiah 21).
Arabia and Kedar traded lambs, rams, and goats with Tyre (Ezekiel 27).
After his conversion Paul went away into Arabia (Galatians 1).
Paul wrote that Mount Sinai is in Arabia (Galatians 4).

aroer_94.name: Aroer
aroer_94.what: A town east of the Jordan near the Arnon River, on Israel's southern border with Moab.
aroer_94.today: Likely Khirbet 'Ara'ir on the Arnon in Jordan; another Aroer lay near Rabbah (Amman).
key: The tribe of Gad rebuilt Aroer (Numbers 32).
Aroer on the Arnon marked the southern edge of Reuben's territory (Joshua 13).
Jephthah struck the Ammonites from Aroer to Minnith (Judges 11).
David's census takers began at Aroer east of the Jordan (2 Samuel 24).
Isaiah foretold that the cities of Aroer would be deserted (Isaiah 17).

arpad_96.name: Arpad
arpad_96.what: An Aramean city-state in northern Syria conquered by Assyria.
arpad_96.today: Tell Rifaat, north of Aleppo, Syria.
key: The Assyrian commander mocked Jerusalem by asking where the gods of Arpad were (2 Kings 18).
Sennacherib's letter to Hezekiah named the fallen king of Arpad (2 Kings 19).
God described Assyria boasting that Calno, Hamath, and Arpad had all fallen (Isaiah 10).
Jeremiah foretold that Hamath and Arpad would be confounded at bad news (Jeremiah 49).

ashtaroth_106.name: Ashtaroth
ashtaroth_106.what: A royal city of Bashan east of the Sea of Galilee, home of King Og.
key: Og king of Bashan lived at Ashtaroth when Israel defeated him (Deuteronomy 1).
The Gibeonites cited Israel's victory over Og at Ashtaroth (Joshua 9).
Ashtaroth was allotted to the half-tribe of Manasseh (Joshua 13).
It was given to the Levites of Gershon's clan (1 Chronicles 6).

babylonia_152.name: Babylonia
babylonia_152.what: The land of Babylon in southern Mesopotamia, where Judah's exiles lived after Jerusalem fell.
key: Sheshbazzar brought the temple vessels from Babylonia to Jerusalem (Ezra 1).
Darius found Cyrus's decree in the archives in Babylonia (Ezra 6).
Artaxerxes let Ezra take silver and gold gathered in Babylonia (Ezra 7).
Family heads went up with Ezra from Babylonia (Ezra 8).

bahurim_154.name: Bahurim
bahurim_154.what: A village in Benjamin just east of the Mount of Olives, on the road toward the Jordan.
bahurim_154.today: Possibly Ras et-Tmim, east of Jerusalem.
key: Paltiel followed Michal weeping as far as Bahurim (2 Samuel 3).
Shimei came out from Bahurim cursing David as he fled Absalom (2 Samuel 16).
Jonathan and Ahimaaz hid in a well at Bahurim (2 Samuel 17).
Shimei hurried from Bahurim to meet David and beg forgiveness (2 Samuel 19).
David warned Solomon about Shimei of Bahurim (1 Kings 2).

beeroth_168.name: Beeroth
beeroth_168.what: One of the four Gibeonite cities, later part of the tribe of Benjamin.
beeroth_168.today: Possibly el-Bireh, near Ramallah in the West Bank.
key: Beeroth was one of the Gibeonite cities that made peace with Israel (Joshua 9).
It was allotted to the tribe of Benjamin (Joshua 18).
Rechab and Baanah of Beeroth murdered Ish-bosheth (2 Samuel 4).
Naharai of Beeroth was Joab's armor-bearer among David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
Men of Beeroth returned from exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).

corinth_306.name: Corinth
corinth_306.what: A wealthy Greek port city and capital of the Roman province of Achaia.
key: Paul stayed in Corinth a year and a half with Aquila and Priscilla (Acts 18).
Apollos ministered at Corinth while Paul was in Ephesus (Acts 19).
Paul wrote to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1).
Paul explained he had spared the Corinthians by not returning yet (2 Corinthians 1).
Erastus remained at Corinth (2 Timothy 4).

cyrene_317.name: Cyrene
cyrene_317.what: A Greek city on the coast of North Africa with a large Jewish community.
cyrene_317.today: Ruins at Shahhat, in eastern Libya.
key: Simon of Cyrene was compelled to carry Jesus' cross (Matthew 27).
Mark names Simon of Cyrene as the father of Alexander and Rufus (Mark 15).
Visitors from the parts of Libya near Cyrene heard the gospel at Pentecost (Acts 2).
Men of Cyprus and Cyrene preached the Lord Jesus to Greeks at Antioch (Acts 11).
Lucius of Cyrene was a prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch (Acts 13).

dedan_329.name: Dedan
dedan_329.what: An Arabian trading people and oasis region southeast of Edom.
dedan_329.today: The al-Ula area of northwestern Saudi Arabia.
key: Dedan was among the nations made to drink the cup of God's wrath (Jeremiah 25).
Jeremiah warned the people of Dedan to flee from Edom's disaster (Jeremiah 49).
Ezekiel foretold Edom's ruin from Teman even to Dedan (Ezekiel 25).
Dedan traded saddlecloths with Tyre (Ezekiel 27).
Sheba and Dedan question Gog's plan to plunder (Ezekiel 38).

east_348.name: The East
east_348.what: The desert lands east of the Jordan, home of nomadic tribes the Bible calls the people of the East.
east_348.today: The Syrian-Arabian desert east of Jordan; not a single site.
key: The people of the East joined Midian and Amalek in raiding Israel's crops (Judges 6).
Their camp lay in the valley like locusts in number before Gideon attacked (Judges 7).
Gideon's pursuit left 120,000 of the people of the East fallen (Judges 8).
Ezekiel foretold that Ammon and Moab would be handed over to the people of the East (Ezekiel 25).

engedi_389.name: En-gedi
engedi_389.what: A spring-fed oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea in the wilderness of Judah.
engedi_389.today: Ein Gedi, on the western shore of the Dead Sea, Israel.
key: En-gedi was one of Judah's towns in the wilderness (Joshua 15).
David hid in the strongholds of En-gedi while fleeing Saul (1 Samuel 23).
David spared Saul's life in a cave at En-gedi (1 Samuel 24).
Moabite and Ammonite armies gathered at Hazazon-tamar, that is, En-gedi (2 Chronicles 20).
Ezekiel saw fishermen standing beside the healed sea from En-gedi (Ezekiel 47).

galatia_431.name: Galatia
galatia_431.what: A Roman province in central Asia Minor where Paul planted churches.
galatia_431.today: Central Turkey, around Ankara and Konya.
key: Paul and Silas traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia (Acts 16).
Paul went through Galatia again, strengthening the disciples (Acts 18).
Paul directed the churches of Galatia about the collection for the saints (1 Corinthians 16).
Paul wrote his letter to the churches of Galatia (Galatians 1).
Peter addressed his first letter to believers scattered in Galatia and nearby provinces (1 Peter 1).

iconium_590.name: Iconium
iconium_590.what: A city in south-central Asia Minor visited by Paul on his missionary journeys.
key: Paul and Barnabas shook the dust off their feet at Antioch and went to Iconium (Acts 13).
Many believed at Iconium, but a plot to stone the apostles forced them to flee (Acts 14).
The believers at Lystra and Iconium spoke well of Timothy (Acts 16).
Paul reminded Timothy of the persecutions he endured at Iconium (2 Timothy 3).

jarmuth_624.name: Jarmuth
jarmuth_624.what: A Canaanite city in the lowland of Judah, west of Bethlehem.
jarmuth_624.today: Tel Yarmut, near Beit Shemesh, Israel.
key: Piram king of Jarmuth joined four other kings against Gibeon and was defeated (Joshua 10).
Jarmuth's king appears in the list of kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).
Jarmuth was allotted to Judah in the lowland (Joshua 15).
People of Judah resettled Jarmuth after the exile (Nehemiah 11).

laodicea_716.name: Laodicea
laodicea_716.what: A prosperous city in the Lycus Valley of Asia Minor, near Colossae and Hierapolis.
laodicea_716.today: Ruins near Denizli, in southwestern Turkey.
key: Paul told the Colossians he was struggling for those at Laodicea (Colossians 2).
Paul asked that his letters be exchanged between Colossae and Laodicea (Colossians 4).
Laodicea was one of the seven churches to receive John's message (Revelation 1).
Jesus rebuked the Laodicean church as lukewarm and called it to repent (Revelation 3).

luz_737.name: Luz
luz_737.what: The original Canaanite name of Bethel, a town north of Jerusalem.
luz_737.today: Bethel, likely Beitin near Ramallah in the West Bank.
key: After his dream, Jacob renamed the city of Luz Bethel (Genesis 28).
Jacob returned to Luz and built an altar there (Genesis 35).
Jacob told Joseph that God Almighty appeared to him at Luz (Genesis 48).
The house of Joseph captured Luz, and a spared man built another Luz elsewhere (Judges 1).

lystra_742.name: Lystra
lystra_742.what: A Roman colony in Lycaonia in south-central Asia Minor, hometown of Timothy.
lystra_742.today: Ruins near Hatunsaray, south of Konya, Turkey.
key: Paul healed a lame man at Lystra, and the crowds hailed him and Barnabas as gods (Acts 14).
Paul was stoned at Lystra and left for dead, but rose and went on (Acts 14).
Paul met Timothy at Lystra and took him along (Acts 16).
Paul reminded Timothy of the persecutions he endured at Lystra (2 Timothy 3).

machpelah_748.name: Machpelah
machpelah_748.what: A field and cave near Mamre that Abraham bought as a family burial place.
machpelah_748.today: Traditionally the Cave of the Patriarchs in Hebron.
key: Abraham bought the field and cave of Machpelah from Ephron the Hittite to bury Sarah (Genesis 23).
Isaac and Ishmael buried Abraham in the cave of Machpelah (Genesis 25).
Jacob asked to be buried there with Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, and Leah (Genesis 49).
Jacob's sons carried his body from Egypt and buried him at Machpelah (Genesis 50).

mamre_762.name: Mamre
mamre_762.what: A place near Hebron where Abraham lived, facing the cave of Machpelah.
mamre_762.today: Near Hebron; possibly Ramat el-Khalil, just north of the city.
key: The cave of Machpelah that Abraham bought lay east of Mamre (Genesis 23).
Abraham was buried in the cave east of Mamre (Genesis 25).
Jacob came home to Isaac at Mamre, where Isaac died (Genesis 35).
Jacob was buried in the field east of Mamre (Genesis 50).

mareshah_767.name: Mareshah
mareshah_767.what: A town in the lowland of Judah, southwest of Jerusalem.
mareshah_767.today: Tel Maresha, near Beit Guvrin, Israel.
key: Mareshah was allotted to Judah in the lowland (Joshua 15).
Rehoboam fortified Mareshah (2 Chronicles 11).
Asa defeated Zerah the Cushite's vast army near Mareshah (2 Chronicles 14).
Eliezer of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat's alliance with Ahaziah (2 Chronicles 20).
Micah warned that a conqueror would come against Mareshah (Micah 1).

migdol_799.name: Migdol
migdol_799.what: A fortified place on Egypt's northeastern frontier, named in the exodus and later a home of Jewish refugees.
migdol_799.today: Likely in the northeastern Nile Delta near Sinai; exact site uncertain.
key: God told Israel to camp between Migdol and the sea before crossing (Exodus 14).
Israel's camp near Migdol appears in the list of wilderness stages (Numbers 33).
Jeremiah addressed Jews living in Migdol and other Egyptian towns (Jeremiah 44).
Ezekiel foretold Egypt's desolation from Migdol to Syene (Ezekiel 29).

millo_802.name: Millo
millo_802.what: A terraced earthwork or fortification in Jerusalem's City of David, built up by David and Solomon.
millo_802.today: Likely the stepped stone structure in the City of David, Jerusalem.
key: David built up the city around the Millo after capturing Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5).
Solomon used forced labor to build the Millo (1 Kings 9).
Jeroboam rebelled against Solomon while the Millo was being built (1 Kings 11).
Hezekiah strengthened the Millo before Assyria's attack (2 Chronicles 32).

mizpah_809.name: Mizpah
mizpah_809.what: A town in Gilead east of the Jordan, named for the watchpost set up by Jacob and Laban.
mizpah_809.today: Exact site unknown; somewhere in Gilead, Jordan.
key: Jacob and Laban made a covenant heap called Mizpah as a witness between them (Genesis 31).
Israel camped at Mizpah to face the Ammonites (Judges 10).
Jephthah's daughter came out to meet him at his home in Mizpah (Judges 11).
Hosea rebuked Israel's leaders as a snare at Mizpah (Hosea 5).

netophah_890.name: Netophah
netophah_890.what: A village near Bethlehem in Judah, home of several of David's warriors.
netophah_890.today: Possibly Khirbet Bedd Faluh, southeast of Bethlehem.
key: Maharai and Heleb of Netophah were among David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
Maharai and Heldai of Netophah led monthly divisions of David's army (1 Chronicles 27).
Men of Netophah returned from exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).

nob_900.name: Nob
nob_900.what: A town of priests in Benjamin just north of Jerusalem, where the tabernacle stood in Saul's day.
nob_900.today: Exact site uncertain; likely near Mount Scopus, north of Jerusalem.
key: Ahimelech the priest gave David holy bread and Goliath's sword at Nob (1 Samuel 21).
Saul had Doeg kill the priests of Nob and strike the town (1 Samuel 22).
Benjaminites resettled Nob after the exile (Nehemiah 11).
Isaiah pictured the Assyrian halting at Nob to shake his fist at Zion (Isaiah 10).

philistia_943.name: Philistia
philistia_943.what: The coastal land of the Philistines in southwestern Canaan, with five major cities.
philistia_943.today: The southern coastal plain of Israel and the Gaza Strip.
key: Moses sang that terror gripped the inhabitants of Philistia (Exodus 15).
God declares that he shouts in triumph over Philistia (Psalms 60).
Philistia is named among nations counted as born in Zion (Psalms 87).
Isaiah warned Philistia not to rejoice at its oppressor's fall (Isaiah 14).

saron_1063.name: Sharon
saron_1063.what: The fertile coastal plain of Israel between Joppa and Mount Carmel.
saron_1063.today: The Sharon Plain along Israel's central Mediterranean coast.
key: David's herds grazed in Sharon under Shitrai (1 Chronicles 27).
The bride calls herself a rose of Sharon (Song of Solomon 2).
Isaiah foretold that the splendor of Sharon would be given to the wilderness (Isaiah 35).
God promised Sharon would become a pasture for his people (Isaiah 65).
Residents of Lydda and Sharon turned to the Lord after Aeneas was healed (Acts 9).

sepharvaim_1050.name: Sepharvaim
sepharvaim_1050.what: A city conquered by Assyria, whose people were resettled in Samaria.
sepharvaim_1050.today: Exact site unknown; possibly in Syria or Mesopotamia.
key: Assyria resettled people from Sepharvaim in Samaria, where they burned their children to their gods (2 Kings 17).
The Assyrian commander asked where the gods of Sepharvaim were (2 Kings 18).
Sennacherib's letter boasted of the fallen king of Sepharvaim (2 Kings 19).
Isaiah records the same Assyrian taunts against Hezekiah (Isaiah 37).

shephelah_1074.name: Shephelah
shephelah_1074.what: The low rolling hills between Judah's hill country and the coastal plain.
shephelah_1074.today: The low hills between Israel's coastal plain and the Judean highlands.
key: Solomon made cedar as plentiful as sycamore trees of the Shephelah (1 Kings 10).
David appointed officials over the olive and sycamore trees of the Shephelah (1 Chronicles 27).
Uzziah kept large herds in the Shephelah and the plain (2 Chronicles 26).
The Philistines raided the cities of the Shephelah in Ahaz's reign (2 Chronicles 28).

shur_1090.name: Shur
shur_1090.what: A desert region in northwestern Sinai along Egypt's eastern frontier.
shur_1090.today: Northwestern Sinai, east of the Suez region of Egypt.
key: The angel of the LORD found Hagar by a spring on the way to Shur (Genesis 16).
Abraham lived between Kadesh and Shur and sojourned in Gerar (Genesis 20).
After crossing the Red Sea, Israel went three days into the wilderness of Shur (Exodus 15).
Saul defeated the Amalekites from Havilah as far as Shur (1 Samuel 15).
David raided peoples living toward Shur while among the Philistines (1 Samuel 27).

teman_1150.name: Teman
teman_1150.what: A region or town in Edom, known for its wise men and warriors.
teman_1150.today: Southern Jordan, in ancient Edom; exact site unknown.
key: Jeremiah asked whether wisdom was gone from Teman (Jeremiah 49).
Ezekiel foretold desolation from Teman to Dedan (Ezekiel 25).
Amos announced fire on Teman (Amos 1).
Obadiah warned that Teman's mighty men would be dismayed (Obadiah 1).
Habakkuk saw God coming from Teman in glory (Habakkuk 3).

thessalonica_1158.name: Thessalonica
thessalonica_1158.what: The chief city of the Roman province of Macedonia, on the Aegean coast.
key: Paul preached three Sabbaths in Thessalonica before a mob forced him out (Acts 17).
Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, sailed with Paul to Rome (Acts 27).
The Philippians sent help to Paul more than once in Thessalonica (Philippians 4).
Demas deserted Paul and went to Thessalonica (2 Timothy 4).

troas_1182.name: Troas
troas_1182.what: A Roman port city on the northwest coast of Asia Minor, near ancient Troy.
troas_1182.today: Ruins of Alexandria Troas, in northwestern Turkey.
key: At Troas Paul saw a vision of a man of Macedonia calling for help (Acts 16).
Paul raised Eutychus after he fell from a window at Troas (Acts 20).
A door opened for the gospel at Troas, but Paul left without finding Titus (2 Corinthians 2).
Paul had left his cloak with Carpus at Troas (2 Timothy 4).

ziph_1266.name: Ziph
ziph_1266.what: A town in the hill country of Judah, southeast of Hebron, beside a wilderness.
ziph_1266.today: Tell Zif, southeast of Hebron in the West Bank.
key: Ziph was allotted to Judah in the hill country (Joshua 15).
Jonathan strengthened David in the wilderness of Ziph, but Ziphites betrayed him (1 Samuel 23).
David took Saul's spear and water jar in the wilderness of Ziph (1 Samuel 26).
Rehoboam fortified Ziph (2 Chronicles 11).

abarim_2.name: Abarim
abarim_2.what: A mountain range east of the Dead Sea, including Mount Nebo.
abarim_2.today: The highlands east of the Dead Sea in Jordan.
key: God told Moses to climb a mountain of Abarim and view the land (Numbers 27).
Israel camped in the mountains of Abarim before Nebo (Numbers 33).
God sent Moses up Mount Nebo in the Abarim range to die (Deuteronomy 32).
Jeremiah told Jerusalem to cry out from Abarim (Jeremiah 22).

admah_27.name: Admah
admah_27.what: One of the cities of the valley destroyed with Sodom and Gomorrah.
admah_27.today: Exact site unknown; likely near the southern Dead Sea.
key: Admah marked part of the territory of the Canaanites (Genesis 10).
The king of Admah joined the cities of the valley in war (Genesis 14).
Moses recalled that God overthrew Admah with Sodom in his anger (Deuteronomy 29).
God asked how he could make Israel like Admah (Hosea 11).

aram_82.name: Aram
aram_82.what: The land of the Arameans north and northeast of Israel, centered on Damascus.
key: Balaam said Balak had brought him from Aram (Numbers 23).
David put garrisons in Aram of Damascus (2 Samuel 8).
Absalom made a vow while living at Geshur in Aram (2 Samuel 15).
Hosea recalled that Jacob fled to the land of Aram (Hosea 12).

athens_118.name: Athens
athens_118.what: The leading city of ancient Greece, famed for its philosophy and temples.
key: Paul preached at the Areopagus in Athens, and some believed (Acts 17).
Paul left Athens and went to Corinth (Acts 18).
Paul stayed alone in Athens and sent Timothy to Thessalonica (1 Thessalonians 3).

beth-shean_233.name: Beth-shean
beth-shean_233.what: A strong Canaanite city where the Jezreel Valley meets the Jordan Valley.
beth-shean_233.today: Tel Beit She'an, in northern Israel.
key: The Canaanites of Beth-shean had chariots of iron (Joshua 17).
Manasseh did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shean (Judges 1).
Beth-shean was in one of Solomon's administrative districts (1 Kings 4).
It is listed among the towns of Manasseh's descendants (1 Chronicles 7).

corner_gate_307.name: Corner Gate
corner_gate_307.what: A gate at the northwest corner of Jerusalem's city wall.
corner_gate_307.today: Exact site unknown; likely at the northwest corner of ancient Jerusalem.
key: Jehoash of Israel broke down Jerusalem's wall to the Corner Gate (2 Kings 14).
Uzziah built towers at the Corner Gate (2 Chronicles 26).
Jeremiah foretold the city's rebuilding to the Corner Gate (Jeremiah 31).
Zechariah described Jerusalem secure from the Corner Gate onward (Zechariah 14).

crete_310.name: Crete
crete_310.what: A large island in the Mediterranean Sea south of Greece.
key: Paul's ship sailed along Crete, and leaving it led to a fierce storm (Acts 27).
Paul left Titus in Crete to appoint elders in every town (Titus 1).

elealeh_368.name: Elealeh
elealeh_368.what: A town on the plateau east of the Jordan, near Heshbon.
elealeh_368.today: El-'Al, north of Heshbon in Jordan.
key: The Reubenites rebuilt Elealeh (Numbers 32).
Isaiah pictured Heshbon and Elealeh crying out (Isaiah 15).
Isaiah wept for Heshbon and Elealeh as their harvest failed (Isaiah 16).
Jeremiah heard Moab's cry from Heshbon to Elealeh (Jeremiah 48).

gibbethon_465.name: Gibbethon
gibbethon_465.what: A town in Dan's territory near Philistine land, later contested with the Philistines.
gibbethon_465.today: Possibly Tel Malot, near Gezer, Israel.
key: Gibbethon was allotted to Dan (Joshua 19).
It was given to the Levites of Kohath's clan (Joshua 21).
Baasha killed King Nadab while Israel besieged Gibbethon (1 Kings 15).
The army at Gibbethon made Omri king after Zimri's coup (1 Kings 16).

gihon_473.name: Gihon
gihon_473.what: The main spring of ancient Jerusalem, in the Kidron Valley below the City of David.
gihon_473.today: The Gihon Spring in the City of David, Jerusalem.
key: Solomon was anointed king at Gihon (1 Kings 1).
Hezekiah closed the upper outlet of Gihon and channeled water into the city (2 Chronicles 32).
Manasseh built an outer wall west of Gihon (2 Chronicles 33).

gozan_492.name: Gozan
gozan_492.what: A region on the Habor River in upper Mesopotamia, where Assyria resettled exiled Israelites.
gozan_492.today: Tell Halaf area, in northeastern Syria.
key: Assyria exiled Israelites to the Habor, the river of Gozan (2 Kings 17).
Sennacherib boasted that the gods of Gozan had not saved it (2 Kings 19).
Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh were taken to Gozan (1 Chronicles 5).

greece_495.name: Greece
greece_495.what: The land of the Greeks, which became a world empire under Alexander the Great.
key: Daniel's vision of a goat represented the king of Greece (Daniel 8).
An angel spoke of the coming prince of Greece (Daniel 10).
A Persian king would stir up all against the kingdom of Greece (Daniel 11).
God promised to rouse Zion's sons against the sons of Greece (Zechariah 9).
Paul spent three months in Greece (Acts 20).

hazeroth_544.name: Hazeroth
hazeroth_544.what: An Israelite camp in the Sinai wilderness after leaving Mount Sinai.
hazeroth_544.today: Exact site unknown; possibly 'Ain Khadra in eastern Sinai.
key: Israel traveled from Kibroth-hattaavah to Hazeroth (Numbers 11).
At Hazeroth Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses, and Miriam became leprous (Numbers 12).
Hazeroth appears in the list of wilderness stages (Numbers 33).
Moses' final speeches name Hazeroth as a landmark (Deuteronomy 1).

jahaz_617.name: Jahaz
jahaz_617.what: A town on the plateau east of the Dead Sea where Israel defeated Sihon.
jahaz_617.today: Exact site uncertain; possibly Khirbet el-Medeiyineh, Jordan.
key: Sihon king of the Amorites fought Israel at Jahaz and was defeated (Numbers 21).
Moses recalled the victory over Sihon at Jahaz (Deuteronomy 2).
Jephthah reminded the Ammonites of Sihon's defeat at Jahaz (Judges 11).
Jeremiah named Jahaz among the Moabite cities facing judgment (Jeremiah 48).

jebus_629.name: Jebus
jebus_629.what: The Jebusite city that David captured and made Jerusalem, his capital.
jebus_629.today: The City of David, in Jerusalem.
key: Jebus, that is Jerusalem, was listed among Benjamin's cities (Joshua 18).
A Levite refused to stay overnight in Jebus because it was foreign (Judges 19).
David captured Jebus and the stronghold of Zion (1 Chronicles 11).

kibroth-hattaavah_685.name: Kibroth-hattaavah
kibroth-hattaavah_685.what: A wilderness camp whose name means graves of craving, where Israel craved meat.
kibroth-hattaavah_685.today: Exact site unknown; in the Sinai wilderness.
key: God sent quail and then a plague on those who craved meat (Numbers 11).
Kibroth-hattaavah appears in the list of wilderness stages (Numbers 33).
Moses recalled Israel provoking the LORD there (Deuteronomy 9).

kir_693.name: Kir
kir_693.what: A distant land, probably in Mesopotamia, from which the Arameans came and to which Assyria exiled them.
kir_693.today: Exact site unknown; likely in Mesopotamia.
key: Assyria captured Damascus and carried its people to Kir (2 Kings 16).
Isaiah also names Kir of Moab, a separate Moabite city (Isaiah 15).
Kir took up the shield against Jerusalem (Isaiah 22).
Amos foretold that Aram's people would go into exile to Kir (Amos 1).
God reminded Israel that he brought the Arameans from Kir (Amos 9).

kiriathaim_695.name: Kiriathaim
kiriathaim_695.what: A town on the plateau east of the Dead Sea, built up by Reuben and later held by Moab.
kiriathaim_695.today: Exact site uncertain; possibly Khirbet el-Qureiyat, Jordan.
key: The Reubenites rebuilt Kiriathaim (Numbers 32).
It was allotted to Reuben (Joshua 13).
Jeremiah announced that Kiriathaim would be shamed and captured (Jeremiah 48).
Ezekiel named Kiriathaim among the glorious cities of Moab facing judgment (Ezekiel 25).

kishon_705.name: Kishon
kishon_705.what: A river flowing through the Jezreel Valley to the Mediterranean near Mount Carmel.
kishon_705.today: The Kishon River (Nahal Kishon), in northern Israel.
key: Sisera gathered his chariots at the Kishon to fight Barak (Judges 4).
Deborah's song says the torrent Kishon swept the enemy away (Judges 5).
Elijah executed the prophets of Baal at the brook Kishon (1 Kings 18).
The psalmist asks God to deal with enemies as with Sisera at the Kishon (Psalms 83).

lebanon_585.name: House of the Forest of Lebanon
lebanon_585.what: A great hall in Solomon's palace complex in Jerusalem, built with rows of cedar pillars.
lebanon_585.today: Not preserved; it stood in Solomon's palace complex in Jerusalem.
key: Solomon built the House of the Forest of Lebanon with cedar pillars and beams (1 Kings 7).
Solomon placed hundreds of gold shields there and used gold drinking vessels (1 Kings 10).
Chronicles records the same gold shields in the house (2 Chronicles 9).

medeba_775.name: Medeba
medeba_775.what: A town on the plateau east of the Dead Sea, south of Heshbon.
key: The Amorites' victory song mentions Medeba (Numbers 21).
The plain of Medeba was allotted to Reuben (Joshua 13).
Ammon's hired Aramean forces camped before Medeba against David's army (1 Chronicles 19).
Isaiah pictured Moab wailing over Medeba (Isaiah 15).

meshech_788.name: Meshech
meshech_788.what: A distant northern people and land, often named with Tubal.
meshech_788.today: Likely in central or eastern Turkey.
key: The psalmist laments living as a sojourner in Meshech (Psalms 120).
Meshech traded slaves and bronze with Tyre (Ezekiel 27).
Ezekiel prophesied against Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal (Ezekiel 38).
God declared he would turn Gog of Meshech back and defeat him (Ezekiel 39).

mount_carmel_831.name: Mount Carmel
mount_carmel_831.what: A wooded mountain ridge on Israel's northern coast, overlooking the Jezreel Valley.
mount_carmel_831.today: The Carmel ridge near Haifa, Israel.
key: Elijah defeated the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel when God sent fire (1 Kings 18).
Elisha went to Mount Carmel after leaving Bethel (2 Kings 2).
The Shunammite woman found Elisha at Mount Carmel after her son died (2 Kings 4).

mount_ebal_832.name: Mount Ebal
mount_ebal_832.what: A mountain north of Shechem, facing Mount Gerizim, where the covenant curses were proclaimed.
mount_ebal_832.today: Mount Ebal, north of Nablus in the West Bank.
key: Moses commanded that the curse be set on Mount Ebal (Deuteronomy 11).
Israel was to build an altar and write the law on stones on Mount Ebal (Deuteronomy 27).
Joshua built the altar on Mount Ebal and read the whole law (Joshua 8).

mount_gilboa_837.name: Mount Gilboa
mount_gilboa_837.what: A mountain ridge at the eastern end of the Jezreel Valley.
mount_gilboa_837.today: The Gilboa ridge in northern Israel.
key: Saul and his sons died on Mount Gilboa fighting the Philistines (1 Samuel 31).
David's lament asked that no dew or rain fall on Gilboa (2 Samuel 1).
Chronicles records Saul's death on Mount Gilboa (1 Chronicles 10).

naioth_873.name: Naioth
naioth_873.what: A place in Ramah where Samuel lived with a company of prophets.
naioth_873.today: Exact site unknown; at Ramah, likely north of Jerusalem.
key: David fled to Samuel at Naioth, and Saul's men and Saul himself prophesied there (1 Samuel 19).
David fled from Naioth to ask Jonathan why Saul sought his life (1 Samuel 20).

ono_909.name: Ono
ono_909.what: A town near Lod in the coastal plain, settled by Benjamites after the exile.
ono_909.today: Likely near modern Kiryat Ono, east of Tel Aviv, Israel.
key: Shemed of Benjamin built Ono and Lod (1 Chronicles 8).
People of Lod, Hadid, and Ono returned from exile (Ezra 2).
Sanballat and Geshem invited Nehemiah to the plain of Ono, intending harm (Nehemiah 6).
Benjaminites lived at Ono, in the valley of craftsmen (Nehemiah 11).

ophel_910.name: Ophel
ophel_910.what: The fortified hill between the City of David and the temple in Jerusalem.
ophel_910.today: The ridge just south of the Temple Mount in Jerusalem.
key: Jotham built extensively on the wall of Ophel (2 Chronicles 27).
Manasseh carried Jerusalem's outer wall around Ophel (2 Chronicles 33).
Temple servants living on Ophel helped repair the wall (Nehemiah 3).
The temple servants lived on Ophel after the exile (Nehemiah 11).

ophrah_914.name: Ophrah
ophrah_914.what: Gideon's hometown, belonging to the clan of Abiezer in Manasseh.
ophrah_914.today: Exact site unknown; possibly near Afula in the Jezreel Valley, Israel.
key: The angel of the LORD called Gideon at Ophrah, where he built an altar (Judges 6).
Gideon made a gold ephod at Ophrah, which became a snare to Israel (Judges 8).
Gideon was buried at Ophrah (Judges 8).
Abimelech killed his seventy brothers on one stone at Ophrah (Judges 9).

pamphylia_918.name: Pamphylia
pamphylia_918.what: A coastal region of southern Asia Minor, with Perga as a main city.
pamphylia_918.today: The Antalya region of southern Turkey.
key: Visitors from Pamphylia heard the gospel at Pentecost (Acts 2).
John Mark left Paul and Barnabas at Perga in Pamphylia (Acts 13).
Paul and Barnabas passed through Pamphylia on their return (Acts 14).
Paul refused to take Mark because he had withdrawn in Pamphylia (Acts 15).
Paul's ship sailed past Cilicia and Pamphylia toward Rome (Acts 27).

pathros_925.name: Pathros
pathros_925.what: Upper Egypt, the southern part of the Nile Valley.
key: Isaiah foretold God gathering his remnant from Pathros (Isaiah 11).
Jeremiah rebuked the Jews living in Pathros for idolatry (Jeremiah 44).
Ezekiel foretold Egypt's return to Pathros, their land of origin (Ezekiel 29).
Ezekiel announced that Pathros would be made desolate (Ezekiel 30).

penuel_931.name: Penuel
penuel_931.what: A place by the Jabbok where Jacob saw God face to face, later a fortified town.
penuel_931.today: Likely Tell edh-Dhahab esh-Sharqi, on the Zarqa River in Jordan.
key: Jacob named the place Peniel, saying he had seen God face to face (Genesis 32).
Gideon tore down Penuel's tower after its men refused his army bread (Judges 8).
Jeroboam built up Penuel as a royal city (1 Kings 12).

pisgah_950.name: Pisgah
pisgah_950.what: A mountain peak or ridge in the Abarim range overlooking the Jordan Valley.
pisgah_950.today: Near Mount Nebo in Jordan; possibly Ras es-Siyagha.
key: Israel journeyed to the top of Pisgah overlooking the desert (Numbers 21).
Balak took Balaam to the top of Pisgah to curse Israel (Numbers 23).
God told Moses to view the land from Pisgah but not to cross (Deuteronomy 3).
Moses went up to the top of Pisgah, where God showed him the land (Deuteronomy 34).

rephidim_996.name: Rephidim
rephidim_996.what: An Israelite camp in the wilderness shortly before Mount Sinai.
rephidim_996.today: Exact site unknown; possibly Wadi Feiran in southern Sinai.
key: God gave water from the rock at Rephidim, and Israel defeated Amalek (Exodus 17).
Israel set out from Rephidim and came to the wilderness of Sinai (Exodus 19).
Rephidim appears in the list of wilderness stages (Numbers 33).

sea_of_galilee_1032.name: Sea of Galilee
sea_of_galilee_1032.what: A freshwater lake in northern Israel, center of much of Jesus' ministry.
key: Jesus called Peter and Andrew by the Sea of Galilee (Matthew 4).
Jesus healed many by the Sea of Galilee and fed four thousand (Matthew 15).
Jesus healed a deaf man in the region by the Sea of Galilee (Mark 7).
Jesus crossed the Sea of Galilee and fed five thousand (John 6).

sibmah_1091.name: Sibmah
sibmah_1091.what: A town on the plateau east of the Dead Sea, famed for its vineyards.
sibmah_1091.today: Exact site unknown; near Heshbon in Jordan.
key: The Reubenites rebuilt Sibmah (Numbers 32).
Sibmah was allotted to Reuben (Joshua 13).
Isaiah mourned the ruined vines of Sibmah (Isaiah 16).
Jeremiah wept for the vine of Sibmah (Jeremiah 48).

tabor_1128.name: Tabor
tabor_1128.what: A rounded mountain rising from the Jezreel Valley in Lower Galilee.
key: Tabor marked the border of Issachar (Joshua 19).
Gideon asked Zebah and Zalmunna about the men they killed at Tabor (Judges 8).
The psalmist says Tabor and Hermon praise God's name (Psalms 89).
Hosea accused Israel's leaders of being a net spread on Tabor (Hosea 5).

tahpanhes_1133.name: Tahpanhes
tahpanhes_1133.what: An Egyptian frontier city in the eastern Nile Delta, where Jeremiah was taken.
tahpanhes_1133.today: Tell Defenneh, in the northeastern Nile Delta, Egypt.
key: Judah's remnant took Jeremiah to Tahpanhes, where he hid stones at Pharaoh's palace (Jeremiah 43).
Jeremiah addressed the Jews living in Tahpanhes (Jeremiah 44).
Jeremiah told Tahpanhes to prepare for Babylon's attack (Jeremiah 46).
